title: University of Osaka Integrates Domestic Superconducting Quantum Processors with OCTOPUS Supercomputer via SEAFOOD Platform - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The University of Osaka's D3 Center and QIQB built SEAFOOD, which links the OCTOPUS supercomputer with domestically built superconducting QPUs, including Urchin with RIKEN RQC chips, through the open-source OQTOPUS cloud stack. It is the first Japanese-made quantum computer integrated with an on-campus supercomputer at a Japanese university. A QSCI proof of concept matched the classical CASCI H4 ground-state energy, formal operation begins December 2026, and up to 10 internal teams get access in FY2027 ahead of JHPC-quantum.

insights.claim: The University of Osaka's SEAFOOD platform links its OCTOPUS supercomputer with domestically built superconducting quantum processors on a separate campus. It is the first integration of a Japanese-developed quantum computer with an on-campus supercomputer at a single Japanese academic institution, with formal operation scheduled for December 2026.
insights.so_what: Japan is building a fully domestic quantum-HPC stack (chips, middleware, HPC) that reduces reliance on IBM or U.S. clouds, so watch Japanese suppliers in this chain.
insights.quote: the first integration of a Japanese-developed quantum computer and an on-campus supercomputer at a single academic institution in Japan
insights.locator: Researchers at The University of Osaka’s
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: SEAFOOD's quantum layer runs QIQB superconducting QPUs on the Toyonaka campus, including Urchin, using chips supplied by the RIKEN Center for Quantum Computing (RQC).
insights.so_what: RIKEN is acting as a domestic chip supplier to other Japanese institutions, an early sign of a home-grown quantum hardware supply chain.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: SEAFOOD splits work across three layers: OCTOPUS classical HPC (2.293 PFLOPS, 140 nodes, 768 GB RAM per node) running Qiskit, QURI Parts and oqtopus-client batch jobs; the QPU layer handling transpilation, pulses and readout; and the OQTOPUS open-source quantum cloud middleware routing circuits and bitstrings between them.
insights.so_what: Supporting Qiskit alongside domestic QURI Parts keeps the platform interoperable, while open-source OQTOPUS could become a Japanese standard for HPC-QPU orchestration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: The OQTOPUS open-source quantum cloud stack used in SEAFOOD was co-developed with Fujitsu, SEC, and TISI.
insights.so_what: Fujitsu's role in the middleware gives it a foothold in Japanese academic quantum-HPC deployments.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: In a Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI) demonstration on SEAFOOD, the Urchin QPU sampled dominant electron configurations of an H4 molecule (1,000 shots) and OCTOPUS's high-memory nodes diagonalized the subspace Hamiltonian, giving a ground-state energy of -2.1147334880 Hartree that matched classical CASCI reference values.
insights.so_what: This validates the integration on a trivially small molecule, not a quantum advantage; the value is in showing the plumbing works end to end.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: SEAFOOD partitions workloads so each processor runs the routines suited to its hardware, with the QPU sampling configurations and the supercomputer doing matrix diagonalization. The aim is strongly correlated electronic-structure simulation for drug discovery and materials, which is expensive on classical clusters while near-term QPUs are limited by qubit count and noise.
insights.so_what: Sample-on-QPU and diagonalize-on-HPC hybrids put demand on high-memory classical nodes as well as quantum hardware.
insights.quote: partitions workloads across a three-layer stack so each processor executes the mathematical routines suited to its hardware design
insights.locator: Simulating strongly correlated electronic structures for
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: In fiscal year 2027, up to 10 University of Osaka research teams will get trial access to SEAFOOD through the D3 Center's proposal-based program, to refine hybrid job scheduling before broader external access through Japan's nationwide JHPC-quantum initiative.
insights.so_what: SEAFOOD is a staging ground for JHPC-quantum, so its scheduling lessons will shape Japan's national quantum-HPC rollout.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: SEAFOOD was supported by Japan's JST Moonshot Goal 6, MEXT Q-LEAP, JST COI-NEXT, CSTI SIP, and NEDO's Post-5G quantum-supercomputer hybrid platform program.
insights.so_what: Several overlapping Japanese state programs are funding quantum-HPC integration, a sustained industrial-policy commitment that supports domestic vendors.
